issues.legal_issue: A validating law that deems a municipal area to have continued within municipal limits is invalid when it does not cure the failure to follow mandatory procedures required for including that area.
material_facts: One village had been proposed for inclusion in the municipality, but no final notification followed; another village was included without the required prior process for inviting objections, and was later excluded.
A final court judgment held that the required procedures for including the villages had not been followed and that their inclusion was invalid.
The validating law deemed the villages always to have continued within the municipal limits, but did not amend or otherwise cure the mandatory procedural requirements that had not been met.
Octroi had been collected from the appellants on the basis that the villages lay within the municipal limits.
issues.conclusion: The validating law was invalid because it deemed the legal status of the villages but did not cure the failure to comply with mandatory procedures for their inclusion.
issues.legal_principle: Under the principle in Shri Prithvi Cotton Mills Ltd. v. Broach Borough Municipality, a validating law must be within the legislature’s competence and must remove the defect that made the earlier action invalid. A statutory fiction deeming a fact to exist carries its inevitable consequences and incidents, as explained in State of Bombay v. Pandurang Vinayak Chaphalkar and East End Dwellings Co. Ltd. v. Finsbury Borough Council, but deeming a legal consequence does not deem the antecedent facts or procedural events needed to produce it. The mandatory procedure for altering municipal limits was not followed, and the validating law did not cure that defect. The judgment also considered M. Venugopal v. Divisional Manager, LIC; J.K. Cotton Spinning and Weaving Mills Ltd. v. Union of India; R.L. Arora v. State of Uttar Pradesh; Udai Ram Sharma v. Union of India; and State of Madhya Pradesh v. V.P. Sharma in addressing statutory fictions and validating enactments.

rule.if: validating_law_case and (mandatory_inclusion_procedure_not_followed) and validating_law_deems_legal_status and not defect_cured

predicates.validating_law_case: The proceeding concerns a law enacted to validate an earlier action that had been held invalid.
predicates.mandatory_inclusion_procedure_not_follow: The required procedure for including the relevant area within municipal limits was not followed.
predicates.validating_law_deems_legal_status: The validating law deems the relevant area to have had a particular legal status without deeming the underlying procedural events to have occurred.
predicates.defect_cured: The validating law removes the defect that made the earlier action invalid.

issues.definition: When a validating-law case concerns a failure to follow mandatory inclusion procedures, deeming the resulting legal status does not validate the earlier action if the law does not cure that failure.
